summary: Andrej Karpathy's 630-line Python autoresearch system where an AI agent autonomously proposes and runs code experiments, evaluates results, and iterates—ran 700 experiments in 2 days and discovered 20 optimizations. Defines the 'Karpathy Loop': propose → execute → evaluate → commit → repeat.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — the continuous self-improving loop concept validates AgentForge's state machine approach, but the specific experiment-running pattern is ML-training-focused, not software development. The loopy autonomous dispatch idea is already tracked in HID-72.

summary: Paper by Alexander Bering proposing a 7-layer memory architecture (working, short-term, episodic, semantic, procedural, core, cross-context) unifying 15 neuroscience mechanisms including dopamine/norepinephrine dynamics, reconsolidation, and predictive memory. Open-source npm packages with 11,589 automated tests.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — far too complex (15 mechanisms, 7 layers) for AgentForge's 1-2 agent run budget. AgentForge already ships skill distillation + planner injection; cross-run episodic memory is tracked by HID-188. ZenBrain's complexity would require months of integration work.

summary: ByteDance's open-source SuperAgent harness built on LangGraph. Orchestrates sub-agents, memory, sandboxes, and extensible skills (defined as Markdown files). Lead agent spawns sub-agents on-the-fly with scoped contexts; sub-agents run in parallel and report structured results.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — the skills-as-Markdown-files approach closely mirrors AgentForge's existing skill architecture. Sub-agent spawning is more dynamic than AgentForge's fixed sequential pipeline. Parallel sub-agent execution was evaluated and deliberately rejected for AgentForge as premature. Skills system already ships.

source: AI Agent Loop Architecture: Triggers, Retries, Checkpoints 2026 (explainx.ai)
summary: 2026 best-practices guide on durable agent pipeline design: checkpointing at stage boundaries, idempotent retries scoped to unique pipeline IDs, retry-vs-fallback distinction, and state preservation to resume from last completed step rather than restarting from zero.
relevanceToAgentForge: High — these patterns are exactly what HID-186 (stage-level partial retry) and HID-167 (automatic retry with failure classification) are designed to implement. Both issues are already open; this source validates the design direction but adds no new capability gap.

summary: LangGraph reached v1.0 in late 2025 (largest enterprise production footprint in 2026, shipped PostgresSaver checkpointer and streaming tool-output API in v0.3.x). Microsoft published AutoGen 1.0 release notes in February 2026 with v2 API as the new default.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — AgentForge uses a custom CLI subprocess approach (not LangGraph/AutoGen), so version bumps in these frameworks don't directly translate to actionable gaps. The PostgresSaver pattern is interesting but AgentForge already uses Prisma + PostgreSQL for state.

source: Recursive Self-Evolving Agents via Held-Out Selection (arXiv:2606.28374)
summary: Research paper proposing agents that self-evolve their own prompts and strategies through a held-out selection mechanism—candidate strategies are generated, evaluated on held-out tasks, and the best strategy is recursively propagated.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — this is research-stage (no production evidence) and requires prompt self-evolution infrastructure. Phase 3 red flags explicitly list 'prompt self-evolution' as a disqualifying pattern. Not feasible in 1-2 agent runs without new infrastructure.

source: State of AI Agent Memory 2026 Benchmark Report (mem0.ai)
summary: Comprehensive benchmark comparing agent memory architectures in 2026: standardized evaluation suite, MemGPT/Letta three-tier model (core/archival/recall), and measurement of episodic vs. semantic vs. procedural memory on the same benchmark tasks.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — standardized memory benchmarks validate the memory investment; AgentForge already ships skill distillation (procedural memory). Cross-run episodic memory is tracked in HID-188. The benchmark data doesn't reveal a new gap beyond what HID-188 already covers.

source: MUSE: A Unified Agentic Harness for MLLMs (arXiv:2606.03005)
summary: A unified evaluation harness for multimodal LLMs (MLLMs) in agentic settings, covering vision-language tasks and tool use across modalities.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — AgentForge is text-only and CLI-subprocess-based; multimodal LLM support is explicitly out of scope for the current architecture. No actionable gap revealed.

summary: O'Reilly Radar survey of the 2026 AI agent infrastructure stack: orchestration, memory, tools, sandboxing, routing, and safety layers. Identifies multi-model routing within single scenarios as a key pattern—fast/cheap model for classification, capable model for generation, shared context.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — the multi-model routing within single scenarios is interesting (AgentForge already routes by role tier per agentModels.ts), but the intra-stage routing pattern (classify with fast model, respond with capable model) could be a future optimization. Backlog is full and this would build on HID-163 telemetry data first.
